headline: Commercialize Proteins.1 as a research-use, single-molecule biomarker instrument company first—anchored in strong academic/IP credibility, validated by head-to-head benchmarking against incumbent bulk methods, and funded through a grants-plus-staged-VC path—before pursuing regulated diagnostics.

applications.application: Oncology, neurology, and immunology biomarker discovery in research labs (rare/low-abundance protein and nucleic acid targets)
applications.rationale: All three peers (Refeyn, Oxford Nanopore, Depixus) launched into these exact research verticals before any diagnostics pivot, using them to build peer-reviewed validation and reference customers.

applications.application: Pharma/biotech target validation and biomarker workflows (as a complement to SPR, ELISA, mass spec, Simoa/Olink)
applications.rationale: Depixus built its go-to-market on drug-discovery target validation with published SPR comparisons; Refeyn expanded from academic characterization into pharma QC/manufacturing use.

applications.application: Multi-omic, single-platform biomarker panels (DNA+RNA+protein from one enzyme-free run)
applications.rationale: Oxford Nanopore's 'richer insights, one-platform' multiomic positioning is directly analogous to Proteins.1's unique ability to read DNA/RNA/protein together—an underexploited differentiator versus single-modality peers.

applications.application: CRO/core-facility characterization services as an early revenue and credibility channel
applications.rationale: Refeyn's ABL Europe partnership and Depixus' pharma reference customers show CRO/core-facility adoption builds both revenue and public validation ahead of clinical expansion.

applications.application: Bridge pilot into regulated diagnostics via a flagship clinical/genomics lab partnership (e.g., rapid oncology or CNS biomarker panel)
applications.rationale: Oxford Nanopore's VCGS ISO 15189 and MATRIX CNS-tumour collaborations are the explicit template for later-stage diagnostics entry once research traction is proven.

market_route.detail: Lead with VTT-originated IP and named academic/scientific co-founders, publishing the seminal physics/method paper, mirroring Refeyn (Kukura), Oxford Nanopore, and Depixus (Croquette/Bensimon) academic-anchor patterns.

Run and publish direct comparison studies against gold-standard incumbents (ELISA, mass spec, Simoa/Olink, SPR/Biacore) with named CRO/pharma partners, as Refeyn did with ABL Europe and Depixus did vs. SPR—this is the single most repeated success factor across all three peers.

market_route.step: Launch a tiered, staged instrument line
market_route.detail: Release an entry-level benchtop system for academic/CRO adopters first, followed by an automated/high-throughput version for pharma QC, plus application-specific software modules per biomarker class (DNA/RNA/protein), following Refeyn's TwoMP→SamuxMP and Oxford Nanopore's pocket→production scaling.

market_route.step: Fund via mixed non-dilutive and dilutive capital
market_route.detail: Sequence EU/Horizon/Business Finland grants and accelerator support alongside seed and Series A/B rounds from specialist deep-tech/life-science investors (IP-commercialisation and biotech-focused VCs), extending runway through the capital-intensive hardware development phase, as all three peers did.

market_route.step: Recruit commercial leadership and protect IP
market_route.detail: Bring in a CEO/COO with a track record scaling single-molecule or sequencing instrument companies (ex-Illumina/Solexa/Sartorius/Danaher-type), while filing core hardware/detection patents early to build a defensible position citable to investors and customers.

market_route.step: Establish a flagship clinical partnership as the diagnostics bridge
market_route.detail: After 2-3 years of research-use revenue and publication traction, pursue one landmark accredited clinical/genomics lab collaboration (ISO 15189-style) in oncology or neurology to pilot the transition from research tool to regulated diagnostic, following Oxford Nanopore's VCGS/MATRIX precedent.

sequence: Years 0-2: solidify academic/IP credibility, publish benchmarking data against incumbent methods, and launch an entry-level benchtop instrument into academic and CRO research-use markets in oncology/neurology/immunology, funded by grants plus seed capital. Years 1-3: build out application-specific software modules per biomarker class, add a higher-throughput/automated instrument tier, and convert CRO/pharma pilots into recurring revenue and reference customers while raising a Series A/B from specialist life-science investors. In parallel, recruit an experienced instrument-company commercial leader and file core IP. Years 3-5: leverage the accumulated publication base and pharma relationships to secure one flagship accredited clinical-lab partnership as a regulated-diagnostics beachhead, only scaling into clinical markets once research-use revenue and validation are firmly established.
